additional_concerns: The legacy-processing provision preserves the existing application process; it does not expressly establish a substantive disqualification from item (ii). The exclusions in node.074087c89e3a3304960f612e, node.1bf6918f69c6b37738daeb83, node.4e6a162c35678e9ddf17ad8e, node.ce439b1cf9ed8301fbb68f94 and node.ea4d19630f8cab09065b1909 remain proposed interpretations, not established consequences. An immutable pending-at-commencement flag also cannot resolve subsequent approval, withdrawal or resubmission.

Node.4d548f2e09bc36ef51212f64 excludes legacy applications from its question rather than deciding their eligibility. Node.b66b3e831bb98a12db59dffa assesses substantive conditions only. Neither supplies an answer about actual relief for a legacy application.
Node.8eb374ffa546ddd2ba291e37 has no executable formalization. Its unresolved actual-relief question must not receive a Boolean answer inferred from substantive qualification alone.

The explicit commencement date supports the date comparison, but the source does not specify a universal assessment-event or implementation-date test. The introductory immediate-effect wording remains unreconciled without the publication date.

The relevant SFC FAQs, any applicable transition guidance and the circular publication date are missing for resolving actual procedural availability and temporal ambiguities. Applicable home-jurisdiction rules are also needed to determine home compliance for a concrete change. The supplied unbound dependency IDs have no identified catalogue mapping or non-null source hash; none can be represented as available or assigned to these authorities by guesswork.
Notification alignment and continuing post-vetting are separate from prior-approval relief. Their exclusion from these typed questions does not establish their removal or overall compliance.

The formulas leave materiality, novelty, complexity, possible local policy implications and home compliance to supplied judgments. They do not implement those legal classifications. The introductory reference to home supervision does not clearly establish an additional independent item (ii) eligibility test.
